ganj-dareh.name: Ganj Dareh
ganj-dareh.summary: A Neolithic settlement in the Zagros Mountains of western Iran, whose name means 'Treasure Valley.'

zagros-mountains.name: Zagros Mountains
zagros-mountains.summary: A 1,600 km mountain range spanning Iran, northern Iraq, and southeastern Turkey, running from Iran's western border to the Persian Gulf.

chogha-golan.name: Chogha Golan
chogha-golan.summary: A Neolithic archaeological site in the Zagros foothills of Iran, notable for the early domestication of emmer wheat around 9,800 years ago.

shulaveri-shomu-culture.name: Shulaveri–Shomu culture
shulaveri-shomu-culture.summary: A Late Neolithic to Eneolithic archaeological culture found in present-day Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia and parts of northern Iran, lasting from about the 7th to the early 5th millennium BC.

susa.name: Susa
susa.summary: Ancient city in what is now Iran that served as capital of Elam and winter capital of the Achaemenid Empire, remaining strategically important through the Parthian and Sasanian periods.

chogha-mish.name: Chogha Mish
chogha-mish.summary: A settlement on Iran's Susiana Plain occupied from about 6800 BCE, which declined once the nearby city of Susa became culturally dominant.

chogha-bonut.name: Chogha Bonut
chogha-bonut.summary: An archaeological site in southwestern Iran settled by around 7200 BCE, believed to be the oldest lowland village in the region and part of early Elamite civilization.

susiana.name: Susiana
susiana.summary: Ancient region in southwestern Iran around the city of Susa, forming the core lowland zone of early Elamite civilization and later organized as an Achaemenid satrapy.

uruk.name: Uruk
uruk.summary: An ancient Mesopotamian city that, at its peak around 3100 BC, may have been the largest urban settlement in the world, with tens of thousands of residents.

golpayegan-county.name: Golpayegan County
golpayegan-county.summary: County in Isfahan Province, Iran, whose capital and namesake is the city of Golpayegan.

kermanshah-province.name: Kermanshah province
kermanshah-province.summary: A province of Iran bordering Iraq, part of the area known as Iranian Kurdistan, with its capital at the city of Kermanshah.

dalma-culture.name: Dalma culture
dalma-culture.summary: A prehistoric culture of north-western Iran from the early fifth millennium BCE, known mainly through pottery excavated at its type site, Dalma Tepe, in the Zagros Mountains.

bulla-seal.name: Bulla
bulla-seal.summary: Inscribed clay, metal or wax token used to authenticate documents and prevent tampering. The oldest ones, from the ancient Near East, were hollow clay balls holding smaller tokens that recorded quantities and types of goods.

tepe-yahya.name: Tepe Yahya
tepe-yahya.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological site in southeastern Iran showing early clay tablet use, early metallurgy and stoneware manufacture.

bampur.name: Bampur
bampur.summary: City in Sistan and Baluchestan province, Iran, serving as capital of both Bampur County and its Central District.

shahr-e-sukhteh.name: Shahr-e Sukhteh
shahr-e-sukhteh.summary: Bronze Age urban settlement in southeastern Iran, dating to about 3550–2300 BC, on the Helmand River. Its rise and fall remain a mystery, and UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage site in 2014.

mohenjo-daro.name: Mohenjo-daro
mohenjo-daro.summary: One of the largest cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, built around 2500 BCE and home to at least 40,000 people before being abandoned by about 1700 BCE.

soapstone.name: Soapstone
soapstone.summary: Soft metamorphic rock, also called steatite, made largely of the mineral talc. It has been used as a carving medium for thousands of years.

uruk-period.name: Uruk period
uruk-period.summary: The era, roughly 4000 to 3100 BC, when the first cities and states arose in Mesopotamia, named after the city of Uruk where innovations like the potter's wheel appeared.

mundigak.name: Mundigak
mundigak.summary: Archaeological site in Kandahar province, Afghanistan, about 55 km northwest of Kandahar. During the Bronze Age it was a center of the Helmand culture.

tall-e-bakun.name: Tall-e Bakun
tall-e-bakun.summary: Prehistoric site in Fars province, Iran, about 3 km south of Persepolis. It was inhabited from before 5500 BC to around 3500 BC.

elam.name: Elam
elam.summary: An ancient civilization centered in western and southwestern Iran, one of the leading political forces of the ancient Near East, with written records from around 3000 BCE.

iranian-plateau.name: Iranian plateau
iranian-plateau.summary: A vast geological and historical region stretching from the Caspian Sea to the Sulaiman Mountains, including ancient Parthia, Media and Persis, and covering much of modern Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

proto-elamite-period.name: Proto-Elamite period
proto-elamite-period.summary: An era in ancient Elam's history, c. 3100 to 2700 BC, recognized as producing the oldest civilization in Iran and featuring an undeciphered early writing system.

karun.name: Karun
karun.summary: Iran's river with the highest water flow and its only navigable one, running 950 km from the Zagros Mountains to the Persian Gulf near the city of Ahvaz.

jiroft-culture.name: Jiroft culture
jiroft-culture.summary: Early Bronze Age archaeological culture of southeastern Iran, centered near the town of Jiroft, proposed as an independent civilization between Elam and the Indus Valley.

kerman-province.name: Kerman province
kerman-province.summary: The largest of Iran's 31 provinces, known in ancient times as the Achaemenid satrapy of Carmania; its capital is the city of Kerman.

tepe-sialk.name: Tepe Sialk
tepe-sialk.summary: A large ancient archaeological site near Kashan in central Iran, linked to the Zayandeh River Culture.

kura-araxes-culture.name: Kura–Araxes culture
kura-araxes-culture.summary: Archaeological culture that existed from about 4000 to 2000 BC across the Caucasus and nearby regions, marked by a sedentary agricultural economy and named after the Kura and Araxes river valleys.

yanik-tepe.name: Yanik Tepe culture
yanik-tepe.summary: A local variant of the Kura–Araxes culture, named for a Chalcolithic and Bronze Age site in Iranian Azerbaijan near Lake Urmia.

lake-urmia.name: Lake Urmia
lake-urmia.summary: A salt lake in Iranian Azerbaijan that was once one of the world's largest saltwater lakes but has shrunk drastically from drought and damming.

pierre-amiet.name: Pierre Amiet
pierre-amiet.summary: French archaeologist and conservator (1922–2021) who specialized in the Ancient Near East.

teppe-hasanlu.name: Hasanlu
teppe-hasanlu.summary: An ancient city site in Iran near Lake Urmia, famous for the Golden Bowl of Hasanlu, whose destruction around the 9th century BC preserved one layer of the city intact.
